shortcut_name: direct reduction to bipartite graph coloring
evidence: deepseek uses "color[v] = 1 - color[u]"; gpt-oss describes "bipartition"; qwen says "Color the graph with 2 colors"; glm maintains a binary "color" array
affordance_in_statement: This tier must be an integer value of either 1 or 2 ... for any two modules u and v connected by a critical link, the product of their assigned tier values must equal exactly 2.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this reduction: with the fixed tier values 1 and 2 and product exactly 2, every link intrinsically requires opposite colors. To defeat the submitted solutions, add a nonlocal validity condition rather than merely rewording the local link rule.

survivor_shortcuts.affordance: tier values are 1 or 2 and every linked pair has product exactly 2

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds connected components, 2-colors them, and chooses the lexicographically preferable orientation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the product condition forces endpoints to receive different binary values

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly identifies the task as coloring the graph with two colors.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: the statement restricts each tier to 1 or 2 and requires product 2 on every edge

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses a visited/color traversal to perform bipartite consistency checking.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: each critical link requires opposite values from the binary tier domain

common_affordance: The binary tier domain combined with the product-2 edge rule is exactly a graph bipartiteness constraint.
recommended_edit: Add a global condition such as: "In addition, the sum of all assigned tier values must be divisible by 3." Example 1 remains valid because its displayed assignment sums to 6, while the submitted solutions will incorrectly accept cases such as n=1, m=0.
